assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near-quantum accuracy at force-field cost and have changed what can be simulated: reactions in solution, materials and biomolecular systems on timescales and sizes previously out of reach. This is a real game-changer for my own field, with consequences already demonstrated quantitatively against experiment.
assessment.attribution: The Behler-Parrinello neural-network potential (2007) is the founding step; Csányi's Gaussian approximation potentials (with Bartók) are the second independent line. Parrinello is the natural anchor, though his name also appears on other candidates. Von Lilienfeld, Weinan E and Bartók made important but more derivative or method-extending contributions, so a three-person cut is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently validated across groups, and universal foundation models are now maturing. Timing is good, though the field is still moving fast.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognize Parrinello through Car-Parrinello or metadynamics instead of this candidate.
Transferability and reliability of foundation-scale potentials outside training data are not fully settled.
Credit between the Behler and Csányi lineages and later deep-learning developments is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling made aryl amines routinely accessible and is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is simple in concept, general and has had enormous consequences, which fits the criterion of a transformative but uncomplicated advance.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general, ligand-controlled catalytic methods in the mid-1990s and beyond; their priority and impact are clear. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor but not the general method, so the two-person configuration is the fairest.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation and industrial use; recognition is arguably overdue, and the field has not been honored by a cross-coupling prize since 2010.
uncertainties: The 2010 cross-coupling Prize may lead some members to see this as an extension of already-recognized chemistry.
Handling of Kosugi's precursor work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a completely new therapeutic modality that reprograms the ubiquitin system with small molecules, with many compounds in clinical trials. It has the new-material, new-concept character I look for.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the first PROTACs (2001), and Crews's group developed the small-molecule versions; Ciulli contributed the VHL ligand and structural-mechanistic understanding. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a separate molecular-glue strand that complicates a three-person cut.
assessment.maturity: Clinical Phase 3 data are only now arriving and approved drugs are not yet established, so this is somewhat early; chemical-biology validation is robust.
uncertainties: No approved degrader drug yet.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together or one strand alone.
Role of Sakamoto and Kim in the original proof-of-concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single nucleotides directly by chemistry rather than double-strand cleavage, and is an elegant, protein-engineering-driven chemical solution with already approved-trial therapeutic consequences. It is clearly a game-changer for genome editing.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader; Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, requiring evolving a new deaminase) were the lead experimentalists, which gives a coherent three-person set. Kondo and Nishida's parallel cytidine deaminase editor is a real priority question.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use began in recent years and independent validation is extensive. Timing is good but the 2020 CRISPR prize may raise concern about overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 Chemistry Prize and with prime editing (B067) that also centers Liu.
Priority of the Kondo/Nishida work.
Whether trainees should be laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory resolved Levinthal's paradox and provides the conceptual framework for protein folding, connecting theory quantitatively to experiments. Its theoretical depth is high, and it underpins the physical interpretation of structure prediction successes.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and collaborators (Bryngelson, Onuchic) developed the funnel/minimal frustration framework; Dill contributed the hydrophobic collapse and lattice-model picture; Fersht provided experimental mapping. Allocation among theorists and the experimental side is genuinely difficult.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation; the folding problem was recognized by the 2024 prize through AI prediction, which may make this either natural complementary recognition or redundant.
uncertainties: Crowded attribution among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill, Bryngelson and Fersht.
Overlap with the 2024 prize.
Whether theory without a single decisive experiment meets the game-changer standard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The d-band model and computed adsorption-energy descriptors allowed catalysts to be predicted rather than discovered by trial, with experimentally verified designs. This is an application of quantitative theory to a practical problem with a clear lineage.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the dominant originator of the descriptor approach; Mavrikakis (Hammer-Nørskov related work) and Rossmeisl are important collaborators. Scheffler's contributions are more foundational DFT surface science and Jaramillo's are experimental validation.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used and confirmed in several catalytic systems, though predictions are still more reliable for trends than absolute rates.
uncertainties: Whether Nørskov alone or with a second laureate is sufficient.
Hammer's role in the d-band model is not on the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable in vivo and enabled siRNA drugs and the mRNA vaccines. The consequences are immense and already demonstrated at global scale.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the key lipid-nanoparticle formulation principles (with Hope and Madden), while MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer made distinct delivery contributions; attribution is crowded and ties to the 2023 Medicine Prize on mRNA modification.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven, but the Medicine prize may be viewed as already having recognized the vaccine impact.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine Prize.
Credit among many industrial and academic contributors.
Which lipid-chemistry breakthrough is decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of the spliceosome across its cycle explain how the intron is excised and give mechanistic insight into RNA-based catalysis, a topic close to ribosome and RNA enzymology that I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann established the biochemical and structural foundations of spliceosome assembly; Shi and Stark contributed landmark cryo-EM structures. Nguyen was key to the first high-resolution structures but a three-person limit pushes toward the group leaders.
assessment.maturity: Structural results are confirmed by several groups; recognition may be seen as natural after cryo-EM, though it could fit biology rather than chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether it would be seen as chemistry or physiology/medicine.
Credit between Lührmann and Shi and the contributions of early splicing discoverers.
